title: The Cedar Forest: Huwawa's Terror
subtitle: Fear, fame, and a dangerous expedition

learningObjectives.text: What does the Yale Tablet say Enlil decreed for the cedar forest?
Why does Gilgamesh say he will enter the forest even if he falls?

terror.work: An Old Babylonian Version of the Gilgamesh Epic
terror.author: Anonymous
terror.translator: Morris Jastrow and Albert T. Clay
terror.locator: Yale Tablet · Column IV; Yale Tablet · Column IV, normalized characters 0-1009
terror.excerpt: To keep safe [the cedar forest], [Enlil has decreed for it] seven-fold terror." Gish [opened] his mouth and spoke to [Enkidu]: "Whoever, my friend, overcomes (?) [terror(?)], it is well (for him) with Shamash for the length of [his days]. Mankind will speak of it at the gates. Wherever terror is to be faced, Thou, forsooth, art in fear of death. Thy prowess lacks strength. I will go before thee. Though thy mouth calls to me; "thou art afraid to approach." If I fall, I will establish my name. Gish, the corpse(?) of Huwawa, the terrible one, has snatched (?) from the time that My offspring was born in ...... The lion restrained (?) thee, all of which thou knowest. ........................ .............. thee and ................ open (?) ........ like a shepherd(?) ..... [When thou callest to me], thou afflictest my heart. I am determined [to enter] the cedar forest. I will, indeed, establish my name. [The work(?)], my friend, to the artisans I will entrust. [Weapons(?)] let them mould before us.
terror.note: Verbatim translation from the named Old Babylonian tablet witness in this edited edition. Brackets and question marks signal textual restoration or uncertainty.

narrativeBlocks.title: A guarded forest
narrativeBlocks.body: In the Yale Tablet fragment, Enkidu warns that Huwawa guards the cedar forest. The danger is described through a roar like a flood, a mouth of fire, and breath of death.

narrativeBlocks.title: Gilgamesh insists on going
narrativeBlocks.body: The translated fragment has Gilgamesh answer that if he falls, he will establish his name. The men then entrust work to artisans to make weapons.

narrativeBlocks.title: The tablet is fragmentary
narrativeBlocks.body: The Yale Tablet translation includes gaps, question marks, and bracketed restorations. Treat the wording as an edited reading of a damaged witness, not an unbroken transcript.

narrativeBlocks.title: Fear and fame
narrativeBlocks.body: This passage stages a tension between Enkidu's knowledge of danger and Gilgamesh's desire for lasting renown.
